verification.notes: Model IDs and adapter flags were read from local help/catalog metadata (codex --help, agy --help, agy models). agy 1.2.7 rejects --effort for claude-opus-4-6-thinking before inference, so that route is model-integrated/default with effort unconfirmed. Terra/Astra have no verified catalog route yet and must not be invented. End-to-end availability remains unverified until the official follow-up test. Worker timeout is a whole-child hard wall; large tasks must split checkpoints or carry an explicit approved per-task timeout. 2026-09-21: verified headless resume flags via --help probes (codex exec resume <session>, agy --conversation <id>, opencode run --session <id>); added timeout tiers, resume policy, routing tiers, and task-sizing guidance. 2026-09-21 (v3): added fixup_policy (new-task-key fixups, cap 2, --fixup-of/--fixup-depth audit flags), ephemeral_worktree policy (Brain creates, launcher never auto-creates; D:\Hermes is not a git repo so worktrees live in target repos), and outer_ring pilot policy (redaction aid with mandatory Brain review; no Cline integration). 2026-09-22 (v4): task_sizing gate (warn 2500 chars, hard cap 6000 with --size-approval; measured on the FINAL prompt post-header; absolute 30000-char Win32 command-line ceiling; thresholds from 25 receipts where all timeouts were >=2550 chars); worker contract header injected by launcher (no worker-side test suites, parseable closing block); same-key resume verification incl. retry auto-verify (zero extra I/O, exact match); stateful fixup depth (depths must follow recorded count 1,2,... under one stable origin id); read_catalog BOM-tolerant; removed duplicate default_timeout_seconds (single source: timeout_policy.standard_seconds). Red-team findings that were REJECTED with reasons: contract idempotency on resume (fresh prompt per call, no duplication), case-folded session compare (CLI replays the id verbatim), NTFS colon worry (fixup_of never becomes a filename), as_posix slashes (universally accepted). 2026-09-22 (v5): per-key total time budget 1200s with unified --timeout-approval escape (also gates a 3rd attempt after 2 prior timeouts; trigger list in receipt.timeout_policy); ledger entries record timeout_seconds; soft timeout-discipline stays a warning only (a 456s success needed its 600s wall); key-text drift kept as procedure guidance, not code (provider prefix-cache micro). 2026-09-22 (v6): CI workflow (Windows matrix 3.11/3.13, suites plus secretscan); read-only Brain-vs-worker usage reporter (receipts plus state.db CanonicalUsage, sections never summed); catalog re-probe procedure (read-only, no inference); streaming stdout reader formally CUT (Windows pipe risk, zero gain on single-JSON adapters); Job Object cleanup deferred to launcher-crash case only (tree-kill already verified in production). 2026-09-22 (v7, benchmark-driven): per-route scarce_resource (Codex/Antigravity burn wall+rate-limit, only Bedrock burns USD); worker contract hardened (implementer identity, no meta-dispatch, no outside reads); receipt.size.prompt_est_tokens floor (chars/4) for killed-turn blindness; verifiability doctrine (crisp spec plus pre-written tests opens Tier-2 directly). 2026-09-22 (v8): opencode-zen-mimo route (MiMo V2.6 Flash Zen free). Provisional xhigh CONFIRMED by single inference probe (20s, full usage telemetry, $0, no adapter rejection); capability bench 10/10 first try in 35s at 11k input tokens with exact scope obedience; synthetic-only retained (free-tier data caution stands regardless of obedience). Session forensics CONFIRMED codex AGENTS.md auto-load contamination (~2.7k chars Brain coordination context as every worker session's first instructions): root cause of recon behavior, NOT model-specific (Luna and Sol both affected); mitigated by launcher counter-instruction plus synthetic_demo/AGENTS.override.md (upstream rejected a disable flag). Killed-turn codex tokens recoverable post-hoc from local thread_token_usage (calibrated exact on live sessions). 2026-09-22 (v9): per-task-key launcher lock (mirrors worktree lock: exclusive create, PID-liveness stale takeover, fail-closed taskkey_busy) serializing budget check, spawn, and ledger append across concurrent launches; dry-runs take no lock. No inference was run for catalog edits.

model_effort_allowlist.notes: Single source of truth for model/effort pairs. IDs verified against provider_models_cache.json (openai-codex models list), `agy models`, and in-repo adapter metadata (agent/reasoning_effort.py, agent/model_metadata.py). The launcher loads this table; it keeps no copy. Unknown pairs are unavailable, never silently remapped.

timeout_policy.scope: whole child worker process, including local commands and tests
timeout_policy.large_task_action: split checkpoint or use an explicitly approved per-task timeout
timeout_policy.total_budget_note: Cumulative spawned walls per task-key may not exceed total_budget_seconds (1200 = two full walls) without --timeout-approval; same unified escape also gates a 3rd attempt after 2 prior timeouts. Forces small tiers first instead of repeated 600s burns.

timeout_tiers.guidance: Draft/small fix: 120-180s. Medium/hard logic: 300s. Standard default: 600s. Above 600s requires --timeout-approval. Smaller tiered deadlines fail fast instead of burning a full 600s black box; the launcher records the tier label in timeout_policy metadata.

resume_policy.budget: resume never bypasses attempt budgets; a fixup after Brain direct tests is a NEW task-key with its own budget, linked via --resume-from-job
resume_policy.timeout_reconcile: resuming a timed-out session still requires prior reconcile plus --reconciled

tier1_draft.use: ordinary drafting, small fixes, first attempt at any bounded phase

tier2_hard.use: complex logic, deep refactoring, architecture work; escalate here only after tier-1 stalls on architecture

tier3_review_paid.use: hard decisions, high-risk review, paid fallback; bounded invocations only

task_sizing.rule: one worker call = one phase (<180s draft, <300s hard). Never dispatch read-everything-plus-implement-plus-test monoliths; split into phase 1 (interfaces/main code) and phase 2 (edge cases/test fixups via resumed session).
task_sizing.gate_note: Launcher warns above warn_chars (receipt.size.oversize_warn) and refuses above hard_cap_chars without an explicit --size-approval note (only a hash is recorded). Thresholds from 25 receipts: all timeouts >=2550 chars (median 3338) vs success median 982. Revisit after N>=100; dense-but-legit payloads (schemas) use the approval escape, not silent chunking.

fixup_policy.rule: A Brain-test failure after a succeeded worker is fixed by a NEW task-key that resumes the prior session (never --attempt-kind retry on the old key). Depth counts consecutive fixup task-keys per origin; after the cap, save a checkpoint and report a blocker instead of opening another fixup.
fixup_policy.timeout_note: 180s fits draft-tier fixups. Hard-task fixups observed at 177-554s must use tier-2 300s, not the fixup default.

ephemeral_worktree.creator: hermes-brain-direct-git-only
ephemeral_worktree.rule: The launcher never creates worktrees. Brain creates a temp worktree inside the target git repo (never under D:\Hermes, which is not a git repo), pre-registers its path in allowed_workdir_roots, then dispatches the worker with --workdir pointing at it. PASS: Brain merges the job branch directly (deterministic git op). FAIL/TIMEOUT: Brain removes the worktree (git worktree remove --force) and deletes the job branch; main stays pristine. Forbidden on the contributor route (exact-workdir lock). Parallel workers require distinct pre-registered worktrees; the single-writer lock still applies per worktree.
ephemeral_worktree.cleanup: git worktree remove --force <path>; git branch -D job-<job_id>

outer_ring.allowed_workdir: D:\Hermes\synthetic_demo only; no new outer-ring dir without a catalog update
outer_ring.rule: Stubs are redaction aids, not air gaps: signatures/docstrings/decorators are dropped or kept per tool output and MUST be Brain-reviewed for leaked logic, secrets in defaults, and endpoint paths before any contributor/external use. Stale stubs (backend changed after generation) are a bug source; regenerate per use.
